case_law.citation: Morgan v. United Retail Inc., 186 Cal.App.4th 1136 (2010)
case_law.holding: § 226(a)(9) requires line-item breakdown of hours at each rate; substantial-compliance defense rejected
case_law.significance: Defeats employer 'aggregate-hours' defense on identity-replacement wage statements

case_law.citation: Jaimez v. Daiohs USA, Inc., 181 Cal.App.4th 1286 (2010)
case_law.holding: Injury under § 226(e)(2) is presumed when required information is absent or inaccurate
case_law.significance: Reverses employer's 'no-harm' defense on missing / false line items

case_law.citation: Willner v. Manpower Inc., 35 F.Supp.3d 1116 (N.D. Cal. 2014)
case_law.holding: 'Knowing and intentional' means employer knew the statement was issued; no specific intent to violate statute required
case_law.significance: Low threshold — every post-2020 ghost statement was knowingly issued
